title: Xuanwu Hospital implants China's first closed-loop responsive neurostimulator, Epilcure, with an on-skull AI chip in a man with drug-resistant bilateral temporal lobe epilepsy (9 Mar 2022)
summary: 9 Mar 2022: Xuanwu Hospital, Beijing, implanted Epilcure, a closed-loop neurostimulator whose on-skull AI chip monitors EEG and stimulates on predicted seizures, in a man with drug-resistant epilepsy.
account: On 9 March 2022 a team at Xuanwu Hospital, Capital Medical University, Beijing, led by hospital president Zhao Guoguang and neurosurgeon Shan Yongzhi, implanted the Epilcure closed-loop responsive neurostimulation system in a man with drug-resistant bilateral temporal lobe epilepsy, the first enrollment in an NMPA registration clinical trial led by the hospital (cnBeta and Kuai Keji, 12 March 2022, both citing the hospital neurosurgery department's WeChat account). The reports describe the device as an artificial-intelligence chip implanted in the skull with intracranial electrodes that monitor EEG rhythms around the clock and, on predicting an imminent seizure, deliver an interfering rhythm to block seizure formation at the focus; bilateral temporal lobe epilepsy is called a relative contraindication for open surgery. The operation went smoothly, the stimulator's indicators worked normally during surgery, and post-operative reconstruction showed precise electrode placement and clear EEG signals (cnBeta). No seizure outcome, patient age or follow-up is reported, and the device's maker is not named.
purpose: Epilcure was built to detect the onset of seizures from continuously monitored intracranial EEG and deliver stimulation to abort them in people with drug-resistant epilepsy; implanting it for that purpose was the intended use, though no seizure outcome is yet reported.
system: Epilcure closed-loop responsive neurostimulation system (brain-computer interface)
deployer: Xuanwu Hospital, Capital Medical University, Beijing
segment: Implanted neuromodulation device in a registration clinical trial
taxonomy_note: Loose fit; the documented outcome is a successful implantation with the device working, not seizure reduction.

ratings.reason: The reports establish a successful implantation with the stimulator working normally and electrodes precisely placed; no reduction in seizures, follow-up or patient-reported outcome is given, so the benefit to the patient's health is not yet established.

ai_role.statement: The hospital, as relayed by the reports, describes the AI element as an on-skull chip that monitors intracranial EEG continuously and predicts imminent seizures to trigger interfering stimulation. The read reports establish only that the implant functioned during surgery and that electrodes were placed precisely; no detection or stimulation event, seizure count or follow-up is reported, so what the AI contributed to the patient cannot be assessed from these sources.
